title: BlueChew reviews: ratings, complaints and FutureClinic - FutureClinic
summary: BlueChew reviews: whether it's legit, an A+ BBB rating beside a 1.1-star customer average, what is in its compounded tablets, and FutureClinic compared.
body_markdown:
BlueChew's seven ED formulas are compounded tablets (chewed and dissolved under the tongue, no water needed) prescribed by affiliated providers on an auto-renewing plan. As of November 2026, its Better Business Bureau (BBB) profile pairs an A+ grade with a 1.1 out of 5 customer average from 50 reviews. Men who prefer an[FDA-approved generic](https://futureclinic.com/blog/ed-treatment-online-sildenafil-tadalafil-no-subscription) at the pharmacy they choose can message a[FutureClinic](https://futureclinic.com/) physician for $40 (or a chosen doctor's listed price, typically $20 to $100), no subscription required.


## Is BlueChew legit?


Yes. BlueChew is the trade name of Dermacare, LLC (345 N. Canal Street, Chicago). Adults 18 and older in all US states except North Dakota complete an online profile and ID upload for review, usually within 24 hours. BlueChew's Terms state "we do not employ physicians or other health care providers." Five Telehealth Medical Group practices provide care; its four-state list (September 18, 2026) names 41 certified nurse practitioners and 8 MDs, and partner compounding pharmacies (Meds Health, LLC; National Treatment Delivery and Care LLC; Curexa Pharmacy) fill orders.


## What do BlueChew reviews say?


As of November 2026, BlueChew's BBB profile pairs an A+ rating (which excludes customer reviews) with a 1.1 out of 5 average from 50 customer reviews, while its blog (November 3, 2026) claims a "4.2 out of 5 rating on Trustpilot from more than 3,200 reviews."


The BBB lists 130 complaints in three years (65 in 12 months), led by billing (38), product (27), service (24) and delivery (20); the BBB marks 111 answered and 19 resolved. Customers report post-cancellation or unrecognized charges, one-time orders becoming subscriptions, promotional price confusion, ineffective tablets, slow support, and missing deliveries. BlueChew's own[legit guide](https://bluechew.com/blogs/lifestyle/is-bluechew-legit) notes the tablets can temporarily tint your tongue blue. Its[reviews page](https://bluechew.com/reviews) lists 263 testimonials without a star average and notes "Results have not been independently verified."


## What is in BlueChew's tablets?


BlueChew's seven compounded formulas use sildenafil, tadalafil or vardenafil, and GOLD adds apomorphine and oxytocin; BlueChew's pages say to chew them, with no water, and its blog calls all but the daily DailyTAD sublingual tablets. As of November 2026, they are **SIL** (sildenafil 45 mg), **TAD** (tadalafil 9 mg), **VAR** (vardenafil 8 mg), **DailyTAD** (chewable tadalafil 9 mg plus seven vitamins), **MAX** (sildenafil 45 mg + tadalafil 18 mg), **VMAX** (vardenafil 14 mg + tadalafil 18 mg), and **GOLD** (Base 70/18/2 mg + 160 IU, High 90/22/3 mg + 200 IU, Extra 110/22/4 mg + 240 IU). Its FAQ also lists caffeine.


BlueChew states its compounded tablets are neither FDA-approved nor generics.[The FDA says](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/human-drug-compounding/compounding-and-fda-questions-and-answers) it does not review compounded drugs for safety, effectiveness or quality before sale. The Viagra and Cialis labels advise against combining ED drugs; a sildenafil-plus-tadalafil trial in 180 men used two separate standard pills. US prescription apomorphine labels cover Parkinson's disease, not ED, and a 2026 Sexual Medicine Reviews paper found limited oxytocin evidence. Vybrique is an FDA-approved sildenafil film that dissolves on the tongue.


## How does BlueChew's plan work, and how do you cancel it?


BlueChew's plan auto-renews monthly (or quarterly for[GOLD](https://bluechew.com/llms.txt) and[DailyTAD](https://bluechew.com/dailytad) ); you cancel via 'Put On Hold' at least 24 hours before renewal under its refund policy or 48 hours under its Terms. Prescription treatments cannot be returned and fees are nonrefundable except under a stated policy. As of November 2026, BlueChew's[product pages list plans from $20 a month](https://bluechew.com/sildenafil) and its blog says $30 a month (tablets from[$2 for DailyTAD](https://bluechew.com/dailytad) ,[$7.30 for GOLD](https://bluechew.com/gold) ); see our[BlueChew vs Hims comparison](https://futureclinic.com/blog/bluechew-vs-hims-for-ed-and-generic-prescription) .
